source_text: Iam igitur tempus est ut ostendamus extra naturae testimonium etiam aliqua auctoritate legis, sic nostra membra fuisse formata, ut alia verecundia, alia libertate gauderent. Ad quod confirmandum Gentium citetur Magister, qui scribens ad Corinthios ait: Corpus nostrum non est unum membrum, sed multa ibus ille mirifice explicavit unitatem consensumque membrorum: "Et quia pauca totius corporis membra nominaverat, atque pro sua honestate genitalia loca directe appellare nolebat
pass_a_gloss: Already therefore time is so-that/as ostendamus outside of-nature testimony also aliqua by-authority of-the-law, thus our members to-have-been formata, so-that/as other verecundia, other by-freedom gauderent. to that/which confirmandum Gentium citetur Magister, who scribens to Corinthios he-says: body our not is one membrum, but many-things ibus that mirifice explicavit unitatem consensumque of-members: " and because few-things totius of-the-body members nominaverat, and for his-own honestate genitalia loca directe appellare nolebat.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law
LS libertas; Blaise moral freedom to will or refuse

pass_b_english: It is now time to show, beyond nature’s testimony, by some authority of the sacred law as well, that our members were formed so that some enjoy modesty and others freedom. To confirm this, let the Teacher of the Gentiles be summoned, who says in writing to the Corinthians: “Our body is not one member, but many” (1 Corinthians 12:14).
Since he had named a few members of the whole body, and out of his own propriety did not wish to name the sexual organs directly…

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

choices.why: Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.
